findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not any sanitizer available for use while drinks were being served. The PIC setup the triple sink testing at 400 ppm (quat) during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a sanitizing solution available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following require cleaning:

(1) The accumulation of debris on the metal shelving in the kitchen by the entrance door (storing the microwave and other equipment/utensils).

(2) The accumulation of debris on the shelves inside of the cooler in the cooler/freezer storage room across from the kitchen entrance (storing various drinks). 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed the cove base has peeled off the wall in the following locations:

(1) Behind the bar hand washing sink.

(2) To the left of the cooler in the cooler/freezer storage room across from the entrance kitchen. 

Ensure that the cove base is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there was not signed employee health reporting forms at the facility. The PIC (person-in-charge) was given a blank copy during the inspection. All people who handle food at the establishment must sign the reporting forms. There will be a follow-up on 08/20/2024 to ensure that all food handling personal have signed the forms.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop at the bar (silver drawer ice storage bin) was stored with the handle in the ice. The ice scoop was moved into a position where the handle was not in contact with the ice during the inspection. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed a cutting board being stored behind the triple sink faucet at the bar. Storing the cutting board in this position poses a risk of contamination from dirty water or soil residues while washing dishes. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are stored in a manner that avoids contamination. Also ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned when contamination occurs. The cutting board was removed from behind the triple sink during the inspection.

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
This is a repeat violation from the 03/31/2023 inspection: Several wiping cloths were observed sitting on the countertops at the bar. Wiping cloths, once wet, must be stored in the sanitizer between uses or placed into laundry if no longer being used. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored properly between uses. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the dish drying racks in the kitchen have an accumulation of soil residue which poses a risk of re-contaminating clean dishes. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the floor behind the stove top has an accumulation of trash, food debris, and soil residues. Physical facilities need to be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 10/12/2022.

Inspector observed that a container of half-and-half in the back of the upright cooler of the kitchen was expired and chunky due to spoilage. Foods were moldy and in unsafe condition during the previous inspection. Ensure that foods are date marked and monitored to prevent foods from reaching becoming spoiled and molding. Operator immediately discarded the spoiled product. Corrected on site. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed items in the walk-in kitchen upright cooler which were missing date marking including but not limtied to diced onions, half-and-half and bread pudding. Ensure that foods requiring temperature control for safety (TCS) are date marked once opened. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Several wiping cloths were observed sitting on the countertops at the bar. Wiping cloths, once wet, must be stored in the sanitizer between uses or placed into laundry if no longer being used. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored properly between uses.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM THE PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 10/12/2022.

The wall behind the triple sink and ice bin the bar has raw, exposed wood present. Ensure that the raw wood is sealed and that a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface is created. Ensure that the raw wood is sealed prior to the next routine inspection in 2023. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that there was a used, dry sponge sitting on the edge of the hand washing sink and steel wool present in the basin of the hand washing sink. Hand washing sinks may ONLY be used for hand washing and no other activities including but not limited to cleaning of kitchen items or dumping of any kind. Steel wool and sponge were removed from the hand sink. Corrected on site. Ensure that hand sinks are accessible at all times and are not used for any other purposes. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several foods which were past the expiration date or in unsafe condition being stored for use including sliced watermelon and milk in an unlabeled Gatorade container which had begun to mold; expired items including French dressing, milk and shelled eggs in the kitchen upright coolers; and expired orange juice in the bar cooler. These items are not safe for consumption. Unsafe foods were immediately discarded voluntarily by the person in charge. Corrected on site. Inspector had an extended conversation with person in charge regarding the condition of food items and the need for vigilance in ensuring foods being used are safe. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following items to be lacking date marking:
- Sliced, actively molding watermelon in the left upright cooler in the back storage room
- Sliced watermelon in the kitchen upright cooler
- Open French dressing without date marking and past manufacturer expiration date
- Open orange juice in the bar cooler without date marking and past manufacturer expiration date
- Open 1/2 gallon of milk in kitchen upright without date marking and past manufacturer expiration date

These items were immediately disposed of by person in charge. Corrected on site. Ensure that date marking occurs with any foods opened and stored for more than 24 hours. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: On arrival, inspector observed that there was no sanitizer prepared in either the bar or kitchen. Clorox wipes were available at the bar and no active food preparation was occurring in the kitchen, but Clorox wipes are not appropriate chemical sanitizer wipes for food contact surfaces. Ensure that appropriate sanitizer is provided at all times of operation with correct concentrations.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the kitchen mop bucket to be filled with waste water. Mop buckets, when moping has finished, must be dumped immediately. This is a repeat violation from the previous inspection. 

6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the kitchen hand sink and the kitchen triple sink had plastic pieces placed along the back but these plastic pieces were cracked/peeling and were not caulked to the wall. These sinks must be caulked and tightly joined to the wall. Ensure that these areas are caulked by the next routine inspection and that materials throughout the facility are smooth and easily cleanable. 

This is a repeat violation from previous inspection. 

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Upon inspection of the bar, inspector observed that there was raw wood behind the triple sink of the bar. Operator states that the raw wood has been there for twenty or more years. Areas subject to moisture such as behind the sink of a bar are required per 2017 FDA Food Code adopted by Illinois and SCDPH in 2019 are required to be constructed of materials that are smooth, durable, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Wood is not an appropriate material in areas subject to moisture. Paint or seal this wood by the next routine inspection to ensure these areas are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable as discussed. 

Floors in the bar are observed to have several cracked tiles with missing portions exposing cement underneath. Ensure that these tiles are replaced by the next routine inspection to create a surface which is smooth and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands – except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved. 

Observed both bar ice scoops to be immersed within the ice basins. Discussed with PIC. Inspector corrected the ice scoops. Ensure the handles stay above the ice so hand contact does not occur between the food (ice) and the surface (ice scoop handle). COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed soda nozzle holder to have a large accumulation of soda debris. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. PIC washed, rinsed, and sanitized the holder during inspection. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed both mops to be stored within the mop buckets and not drying in a manner that allows to drip and/or air dry. Ensure mops are stored properly between uses. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter

Observed mop water within both mop buckets. Ensure mop water is disposed of in a proper mop water disposal area such as a mop/utility sink. Ensure water is disposed of after each mop use. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the kitchen hand sink and the 3 compartment sink to lack caulk between the sinks and wall. Ensure caulking before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses for employees. Ensure all employees who work the bar and/or kitchen have food handlers licenses. Provide copies and leave at the facility.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Notice to correct: Absence of chemical test kit to check sanitizer of the third sink of the bar. Replace the chemical test kit.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
When remodeled: Ceiling tile in the bar areas pitted and absorbant. Replace the ceiling tile with smooth and easily cleanable tile when remodeled.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of Scrubbing bubbles on the top of the beer cooler. Employee removed the bottle and placed it with other chemicals.(Corrected)
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the cutting boards to have many nicks, cuts, grooves in the plastic surface. (Corrected)-thrown away. Replace the cutting boards.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
REPEAT VIOLATION: Absence of chemical test strips to check the sanitizer in the bar sink, as well as the 3 compartment sink. Provide a chemical test kit.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed both restrooms to be without covered receptacles for each stall. Provide covered receptacles.
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
WHEN REMODELED: Ceiling tile in the bar area is pitted and absorbant. Replace the ceiling tile with smooth and easily cleanable tile when remodeled.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.
Ceiling tile in the kitchen ajar in the kitchen (2) tiles. Repair the tile.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed Lysol spray bottles on top of the ice machine  and on the top of the beer coolers. (Corrected)Store chemicals with chemicals and away from food.(ice)
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.
